title: Cozmo stack source-fidelity manifest
about: One record per behaviour-affecting decision, or tightly bound group of decisions, in the hand-written
production code of cozmo-stack. Platform plumbing that cannot change what the robot does (logging,
collection choices, string formatting, file layout) is not recorded.
The manifest, not the prose documents, is the authoritative statement of what rests on primary source.
re-analysis/tools/fidelity.py validates it and regenerates FIDELITY_GAPS.md from it.
authority_order: the decompiled Unity C# (unity/scripts/csharp) and managed assemblies
the shipped Wwise banks, their .txt definition files, SoundbanksInfo.xml and PluginInfo.xml
the shipped OBB assets, configuration and animation data
CLAD / message schemas and the code generated from them
captures taken from the original app (re-analysis/captures)
existing reverse-engineering notes, only after checking them against the primary evidence above

statuses.EXACT_SOURCE: Read from primary source and reproduced. The record names the address, asset or schema it was read from.
statuses.EQUIVALENT_IMPLEMENTATION: The native behaviour is known from primary source and this stack reaches the same observable effect by a different mechanism. The record names the difference, and the difference has to be one a listener, a viewer or the robot cannot tell apart.
statuses.RECOVERABLE_GAP: A behaviour-affecting decision whose answer plausibly exists in primary source that has not been read, or has been read too shallowly to settle it. The work outstanding is reverse engineering.
statuses.IMPLEMENTATION_GAP: The native behaviour is established from primary evidence, and the production implementation knowingly does something else. The work outstanding is building it. This is unfinished fidelity work, not a policy.
statuses.COMPATIBILITY_POLICY: A deliberate product or platform decision this stack intends to keep: offline tools, the test harness, PC-side plumbing, or a stand-in the operator has to ask for. Not a place to put fidelity work that is hard.
statuses.HARDWARE_ONLY: No shipped artifact can settle it; only a robot, or a recording of the stock app, can.
statuses.BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: The answer lies in third-party code or data that is not in the package (Omron OKAO, the Wwise runtime DSP, the Acapela text-to-speech engine).

gate.rule: Two separate questions, and neither may be answered by the other. A subsystem's source investigation is exhausted only when it holds no RECOVERABLE_GAP on a live execution path; its implementation fidelity is complete only when it holds no IMPLEMENTATION_GAP there. A subsystem can have exhausted the source and still not reproduce what the source says, and neither state means the behaviour is faithfully reproduced: BLOCKED_EXTERNAL and HARDWARE_ONLY items can remain in both cases, and are counted separately so that they cannot be lost behind a single word.

field_notes.location: repository-relative path, optionally with :line, of the code the record is about
field_notes.effect: what a listener, viewer or the robot would observe if this decision were wrong
field_notes.provenance: what the current implementation actually rests on
field_notes.authority: the best available original evidence for this decision
field_notes.evidence: concrete references: native addresses, asset paths, bank object ids, capture files
field_notes.unresolved: for a RECOVERABLE_GAP, what has still to be read; for an IMPLEMENTATION_GAP, what has still to be built; empty string when nothing is
field_notes.hardware_required: whether a robot is genuinely needed to settle it
field_notes.live_path: whether the decision is reached on a normal run against a robot
field_notes.test: the regression that would fail if the recovered behaviour were undone

records.title: Only a ping marked as a reply measures the round trip
records.authority: ReliableConnection::ReceivePing 0x00835C70 branches on the byte at payload+0x10. Non-zero: the round trip is now - payload.timeSent, warned about if negative ("Ping has returned before it was sent!?") and added to a RecentStatsAccumulator sized by sMaxPingRoundTripsToTrack. Zero: the engine answers with SendPing(transport, payload.timeSent, true), but only when sSendSeparatePingMessages is set, and measures nothing. There is no third case
evidence: the payload is 17 bytes: f64 timeSent, u32 numPingsSent, u32 numPingsReceived, u8 isReply, and SendPing 0x00835BF2 writes exactly that, sending it as message type 0x0B
the counter bookkeeping matches too: numPingsReceived is incremented on receipt, and the pair is kept only when the incoming numPingsSent exceeds the last one seen

this stack also treated an echo of a timestamp it had sent as a reply, on the strength of a PyCozmo capture of the robot echoing with isReply clear. Against such a robot the app measures no round trip at all, so that clause is gone

records.title: The frame payload bound is the engine 1406
records.authority: RobotConnectionManager::Init calls UDPTransport::SetMaxNetMessageSize(0x58C) = 1420 at 0x0062EFC6, after SetHeaderPrefix(4 bytes) and SetDoesHeaderHaveCRC(false). The reliable payload per frame is 1420 less the 4-byte prefix and the 10-byte header, so 1406
evidence: the static default UDPTransport::sMaxNetMessageSize is 0x5C0 = 1472; the robot connection lowers it to 1420

this stack had 1037, from a PyCozmo robot-side measurement. Nothing in the package supports it, the shipped app plainly sends up to 1406, and what PyCozmo was measuring is not established; it is not authority over the app own transport
the multipart split follows from the bound rather than from a number written into the test

records.title: The connect sequence, and the constant in SyncTime second word
records.authority: RobotInitialConnection::OnNotified sends GetManufacturingInfo (0x0052DE6C). On a successful RobotConnectionResponse, RobotEventHandler::HandleMessage 0x005289AC calls Robot::SyncTime 0x0051521E, which clears the state history and calls SendSyncTime 0x0051524C; that sends SyncTime and then, only if the SyncTime send succeeded, InitController (0x0051529A). So the order this stack uses - GetManufacturingInfo, SyncTime, InitController - is the engine order
evidence: SendSyncTime builds the message from BaseStationTimer::GetCurrentTimeStamp() and the literal 0xC1A00000, which is -20.0f (movs r0,#0 / movt r0,#0xc1a0 at 0x0051526C). This stack sent zero in that word
after SyncTime the engine also queues SetReadyToStreamAnims

records.title: The light colour word: 5-5-5 with red at bit 10, and bit 15 set from the alpha byte
records.authority: CubeLightComponent::SendTransitionMessage 0x00638056 packs the engine ColorRGBA word whole: mov.w ip,#0x7c00 / mov.w r3,#0x3e0 / and.w r4,ip,r5,lsr #17 (red bits 27..31 to bit 10) / and.w r7,r3,r5,lsr #14 (green bits 19..23 to bit 5) / ubfx r4,r5,#0xb,#5 (blue bits 11..15 to bit 0) / tst.w r5,#0xff with orrne r7,r7,#0x8000 (bit 15 from the alpha byte). ColorRGBA holds red in the top byte and alpha in the bottom, which CubeLightComponent::WhiteBalanceColor 0x0063a894 confirms by reading the low byte as the alpha it gates on
evidence: CubeLightComponent::WhiteBalanceColor 0x0063a894 treats the low byte as alpha

every colour in every shipped light config has a non-zero alpha - cube configs write [r,g,b,255] and backpack configs [r,g,b,1] - so the engine sets bit 15 on every word it sends, the black that turns a light off included

records.title: Every field of DockWithObject, read from the engine that fills it
records.authority: three functions settle the whole 21 bytes. IDockAction::CheckIfDone 0x005521AC is the only caller of DockingComponent::DockWithObject 0x0063BA44, which is the only caller of the builder at 0x0063BD50, which is the only place the message is constructed. Word 0 is a literal zero (movs r4,#0 / str r4,[sp,#0x1c], and the builder dereferences that local into it). Words 1 to 3 are IDockAction +0xAC, +0xB0, +0xB4, named by SetSpeed 0x00550426, SetAccel 0x00550432 and SetSpeedAndAccel 0x00550416, defaulting to 60, 200 and 500. Byte 4 is the DockAction at +0x80. Byte 5 is +0x95, the IDockAction constructor bool, which also picks tracks 7 or 3. Byte 6 is +0xBA, cleared by the constructor and written by nothing else. Byte 7 is the docking method at +0xBB, named by DriveToPickupObjectAction::SetDockingMethod 0x0055C5A2. Byte 8 is +0xC1
evidence: builder 0x0063BD50; caller 0x0063BA44; only caller of that 0x005521AC
IDockAction constructor 0x005502D8 defaults: speed 60 (0x42700000), accel 200 (0x43480000), decel 500 (0x43FA0000), +0xBA 0, +0xBB 0, +0xC1 0
PickupObjectAction 0x005536EA writes +0xBB = 2 and 0x005536F8 writes +0xC1 = 1; RollObjectAction 0x005565DC writes DockAction 5, which matches this stack RollLow = 5
the three speeds were being written one word early, so every dock this stack sent carried its speed in word 0 and no deceleration at all; robot acceptance had not caught it

records.title: Letting go of a carried object leaves it Dirty where the lift left it
records.authority: CarryingComponent::SetCarriedObjectAsUnattached(bool) 0x006333D4 takes the object pose with respect to the robot and hands it to ObjectPoseConfirmer::AddRobotRelativeObservation(object, pose, PoseState 2) at 0x00633458, so the object stays located, at the pose it was released at, and Dirty. The bool decides whether that survives: set, 0x00633930 also runs BlockWorld::DeleteLocatedObjects and the object goes
evidence: BehaviorPutDownBlock passes false (0x005C84CE), so a put-down leaves the cube where it was put
PickupObjectAction::Verify passes true (0x00553CAA, 0x00553D2A), because a pick-up that turned out to have failed leaves nobody knowing where the cube is
this stack only cleared a flag: the cube stayed Known at whatever pose it last had

records.title: The two timed checks a pick-up is verified against
records.authority: PickupObjectAction::Verify 0x00553BE0 stamps the time of its first call at +0x10C and then runs two checks, both ending in CarryingComponent::SetCarriedObjectAsUnattached(true). At 0x00553C98, if the object still reports itself moving and more than +0x118 = 500 ms have passed since the stamp, the pick-up failed ("PickupObjectAction.Verify.ObjectStillMoving"). Otherwise, at 0x00553D0A, the stamp must not be later than the object last-observed time plus a timeout chosen by the dock action at +0x80: +0x11C = 500 ms for a low dock, +0x120 = 2000 ms for a high one. The constructor sets all four at 0x005536CC onwards
evidence: the object is asked whether it is moving through a virtual on ObservableObject (0x00553C8E), which is why the flag lives on the object here rather than in a tracker beside it
the same function also holds the checks this stack already had: carrying, and seeing the object still in its original pose

records.title: The pose chain that holds a carried object
records.authority: Robot::Robot 0x0050FBF0 builds the tree: a lift pivot at robot+0x2E4, child of the robot origin at translation (-41, 0, 45) - 0xC2240000, 0, 0x42340000 at 0x0050FFE0 - and the lift pose at robot+0x2F0, child of the pivot at (66, 0, 0) (0x42840000 at 0x00510038). Robot::ComputeLiftPose 0x005151AC swings that arm about Y by the lift angle and rotates the orientation back by the same angle, so the plate stays level. CarryingComponent::SetObjectAsAttachedToLift 0x00632CC4 then places the object with respect to the lift pose at (|dockMarkerOffset| + 4, 0, -12.5): it takes the norm of the dock marker translation on the object at 0x00632E42 and pairs it with -12.5 (0xC1480000 at 0x00632E82)
evidence: 45 and 66 are the numbers the height conversion already used, and the chain reproduces it exactly: 45 + 66 sin(angle) is what Robot::GetLiftHeight reports
the -41 was the missing one, which is why a carried cube could not be placed from the lift height alone
the object was not being placed at all before this: the world model held it where it was last seen on the table for as long as the robot carried it
the same function calls FindObjectOnTopOrUnderneathHelper with 15.0 (0x41700000), which is the stack tolerance M13-007 records

records.title: The dock helper allows two attempts
records.authority: PickupBlockHelper::RespondToPickupResult reads the attempt count at helper+0x108 and takes the retry branch only while it is 1 or less (cmp r0, #1 / bls at 0x005B8192). The log beside it is built with a literal 2 (movs r6, #2 at 0x005B814A), so it reads "attempt 1 / 2" then "attempt 2 / 2". The count is zeroed in the constructor and in Init
evidence: this stack allowed three, so it kept trying after the app would have given up

the roll helper does not hard-code its limit: StartRollingAction 0x005B9F62 compares the count against a value carried in its RollBlockParameters, so the roll and charger limits are a separate question - see M12-016

records.title: The search-for-block pattern is recovered and not built
records.effect: the robot stops where the app would look around for the cube
records.provenance: nothing: this stack gives up instead of searching
records.authority: SearchForBlockHelper::SearchForBlock 0x005BAF24 is a three-state machine, and all three states are read. State 0 (0x005BAF9A): SearchForNearbyObjectAction(target, -0.0872665 rad = -5 degrees of head angle, 100.0, -20.0), followed by TurnTowardsObjectAction(target, Radians(pi)) when the target id is set. State 1 (0x005BB1AA): DriveStraightAction(-20 mm at 20 mm/s), TurnInPlaceAction(+0.785398 = +45 degrees) twice, another SearchForNearbyObjectAction on the same three numbers, then the drive again. State 2 (0x005BB066) is the mirror: the same drive with TurnInPlaceAction(-0.785398 = -45 degrees) twice. SearchForNearbyObjectAction 0x005469C0 defaults its search angle to 0.261799..0.349066 rad (15..20 degrees) and its wait to 0.8..1.2 s, with SetSearchAngle and SetSearchWaitTime as the setters
evidence: SearchForBlockHelper::ShouldBeAbleToFindTarget 0x005BB73C decides whether searching is worth it: ObservableObject::IsVisibleFromWithReason with 0.785398 rad, checking the reason against 7
every action the pattern needs already exists in this stack except the nearby-object search
records.unresolved: the three states have to be built, and SearchForNearbyObjectAction with them; nothing is left to read for the pattern itself

records.authority: DriveToObjectAction::CheckIfDone 0x00559880 loads 0x04000001 into r8 at 0x005598E2, compares the distance from the pre-action pose against the tolerance at +0x84, and on the failing side moves r8 into the result (0x005599FE) beside a warning; the passing side returns 0

records.title: What makes a cube a valid bottom to stack on: resting flat within ten degrees
records.authority: DockingComponent::CanStackOnTopOfObject 0x0063C5C4 is CanInteractWithObjectHelper 0x0063C654 followed by !IsPoseTooHigh(pose, 1.0, 15.0, 0.5). The helper checks the object is located and then IsRestingFlat(Radians(0.174533)) - ten degrees (0x3E32B8C2 at 0x0063C670). ObservableObject::IsRestingFlat 0x0087751C asks GetRotatedParentAxis for the parent axis the object own Z lies closest to and returns acos(|dot|) < tolerance
evidence: the absolute value is the point: a cube resting on any of its six faces is flat, and only one balanced on an edge or a corner is not

there is no progression unlock and no uprightness flag in the path; the record had supposed both. This stack tested UpAxisFromPose() == ZPositive, which refuses a cube lying on its side that the engine would happily stack on
the 15.0 in the height check is the same stack tolerance M13-007 records

records.title: DockingErrorSignal begins with the timestamp, not the geometry
records.authority: DockingComponent::UpdateDockingErrorSignal 0x0063BE80 builds the struct at sp+0xa0. Its only argument is the timestamp - mov r6, r1 at 0x0063BE92, unchanged until 0x0063C17E - and str r6, [sp, #0xa0] at 0x0063C14A writes it into word 0. x follows at +0xa4, y at +0xa8, z at +0xac and the angle at +0xb0, and DockingErrorSignal::Pack 0x007C0B26 reads five words then two bytes
evidence: the name table matched the 16-byte VizInterface::DockingErrorSignal by prefix, which put x_dist in word 0 and shifted every field of this 22-byte message by one word
the geometry itself was already right: x - placementOffsetX, y + placementOffsetY, z, and yaw of the flat-clamped pose + pi/2 + the placement offset angle

records.title: The docking error signal's last two bytes are whatever was on the engine's stack
records.effect: two bytes of every error signal differ from the ones the app sent
records.provenance: this stack sends zero
records.authority: UpdateDockingErrorSignal 0x0063BE80 is the only builder and it never writes the struct bytes at +0x14 and +0x15. Nothing clears the struct either: it is a stack local at sp+0xa0 filled field by field, with no memclr and no constructor call, and Pack 0x007C0B26 reads both bytes and sends them
evidence: the engine value is indeterminate, so the robot cannot be acting on it; sending zero is as faithful as any other value and is at least repeatable
the other twenty bytes are exact - see M12-013

records.title: PlaceObjectOnGround sends three zero offsets and a constant speed triple
records.authority: the builder at 0x00632B88, reached only from CarryingComponent::PlaceObjectOnGround 0x00632A88. The first three words are integer locals the caller sets to zero, converted with vcvt.f32.s32; the next three are a constant triple at 0xC7CD90 - 100, 200, 500 - and the last byte is the component bool argument
evidence: the speeds are not the path motion profile: they are fixed in rodata

records.title: Obstacle padding and the soft-ring penalty
records.effect: paths hug or avoid obstacles differently, and some plans fail that would succeed
records.provenance: a padding radius and penalty weight chosen here
records.authority: the mechanism is settled. AddObstacleAllThetas(quad, penalty) 0x008549E0 builds a FastPolygon from the quad and copies it once per theta bucket, storing the penalty argument at entry+0x44 of each 72-byte entry (vstr s16, [sp, #0x5c] at 0x00854A70, the entry being built at sp+0x18). GetCollisionPenalty 0x008517B0 walks the bucket for the state theta and returns the +0x44 of the first polygon containing the point. So the penalty is per obstacle and supplied by whoever adds it, and the hard and soft rings are separate obstacle sets (IsInCollision 0x008515BC against IsInSoftCollision 0x00851708)
evidence: LatticePlannerImpl::ImportBlockworldObstaclesIfNeeded 0x004FD4B8 carries the pair it uses and logs it: 7.0 and 6.0, or 2.0 and 1.0 when its bool argument is set (0x004FD4EE)
neither AddObstacleAllThetas overload has a direct caller, so the import expands the obstacles itself rather than going through them
records.unresolved: which of the two floats is padding and which is penalty, and how the import turns an object bounding box into the hard and soft polygons - the expansion is inlined into ImportBlockworldObstaclesIfNeeded rather than going through AddObstacleAllThetas

records.title: The primitive file states the arcs and the turn costs outright
records.authority: config/engine/cozmo_mprim.json, which xythetaEnvironment::ReadMotionPrimitives 0x008529C0 loads and MotionPrimitive::Create 0x00853DD0 parses. Its nine actions carry an extra_cost_factor each: 1.0001 short straight, 1.0 long straight and all four arcs, 2.0 both in-place turns, 1.2 the backwards short straight (which also sets reverse_action). Each of the 9 primitives per starting angle carries straight_length_mm and, for the four turning ones, an arc block with centerPt_x_mm, centerPt_y_mm, radius_mm, startRad and sweepRad
evidence: the arcs are exact: a slight turn is 7.639 mm of straight into a 94.72135955 mm radius through 0.4636476090 rad, a hard one 5.858 mm into 34.14213562 mm through 0.7853981634, and each arc closes on its end cell to within a thousandth of a millimetre
the arc is stored already rotated for its starting heading - the same slight left at heading 90 has its centre at (-94.721, 7.639) with startRad 0 - so it is translated, never rotated
this stack derived the radius and the straight length from the end cell and called the reconstruction INFERRED; both were in the file all along

records.title: The whiteboard keeps a list of beacons and the active one is the first
records.authority: AIWhiteboard::AddBeacon 0x0056C39C appends to a vector<AIBeacon> at whiteboard+0x60, twenty bytes an entry (a Pose3d, a float radius at +0xC and an int at +0x10), growing it through __emplace_back_slow_path when it is full. records.title: The stack tolerance is 30 mm when building a stack and 15 mm everywhere else
records.authority: BlockWorld::FindObjectOnTopOrUnderneathHelper 0x0062601C takes the tolerance as its second argument, and the callers do not agree on one number. BlockConfigurations::StackOfCubes::BuildTallestStackForObject passes 30 (0x41F00000 at both 0x0061928C and 0x00619344); BlockWorld::UpdatePoseOfStackedObjects 0x00621908, DockingComponent::CanInteractWithObjectHelper 0x0063C728 and CarryingComponent::SetObjectAsAttachedToLift 0x00632F0C all pass 15 (0x41700000)
evidence: the helper takes the object height along the parent Z through GetDimInParentFrame and looks for a neighbour whose centre sits that far above or below, within the tolerance
this stack used 15 for building the stack list, which is the tighter of the two

records.title: The mount is decided by the heading after the reverse, not by the contacts during it
records.authority: MountChargerAction::CheckIfDone 0x0054E2D0 runs the turn-and-mount sub-action to completion and only then looks at the world: it takes the charger yaw (0x0054E344) and the robot yaw (0x0054E358), subtracts, takes the absolute value and compares against pi/2 (0x3FC90FDB at 0x0054E374). Inside the window the mount stands; outside it, or with the charger no longer located, it warns "Turning and mounting the charger failed" and runs ConfigureDriveForRetryAction, whose completion returns 0x04000006
evidence: nothing in the path watches the charger contacts while the robot reverses; this stack raced the drive against the contacts report and aborted the path on the first IS_ON_CHARGER
DriveOffChargerContactsAction 0x005582E4 works the same way in the other direction: it drives its 10 mm in full and only warns if the contacts still report afterwards

the engine compares the charger pose own yaw, which matches a docked robot only under one of the two charger conventions; which one is the open half of M13-009, so this stack measures the window against the docked heading it computes rather than guessing

records.title: The charger dimensions and the docked pose, with the pre-dock pose still unread
records.effect: the robot aims at the wrong point when mounting
records.provenance: the pre-dock pose is this stack own: on the charger axis, facing the marker, at the distance the mount action aligns to
records.authority: Charger::Charger 0x004E9B6C settles the object: 96 x 80 x 31 mm stored at +0xF0 (0x42C00000, 0x42A00000, 0x41F80000) and one marker added with a pose rotated -90 degrees about Z (0xBFC90FDB) at (86, 0, 22) - 0x42AC0000 and 0x41B00000, which is 22 and not the 11 this stack had - sized 20 x 27 (0x41A00000, 0x41D80000). Charger::GetRobotDockedPose 0x004EA1A0 is a single branchless function: Pose3d(Radians(3.14159), Z_AXIS, (30, 0, 0)) on the charger pose, so a docked robot faces out, half a turn from the charger heading, 30 mm along its +X. Charger::GeneratePreActionPoses 0x004E9FB0 has not been read through
evidence: the marker height was wrong by half, which moves where the charger is placed from a sighting

the docked pose being chargerYaw + pi sits awkwardly against the mount check in M13-008, which compares the charger yaw with the robot yaw against pi/2; both readings are from source and they cannot both mean what they appear to
records.unresolved: Charger::GeneratePreActionPoses, which is the pre-dock pose the mount aligns to; and the contradiction between GetRobotDockedPose and the mount heading check

records.title: The workouts run in file order and the last one repeats
records.authority: WorkoutComponent::GetCurrentWorkout 0x00573DE8 returns a pointer kept at +0xC - it selects nothing. CompleteCurrentWorkout 0x00573DEC fires the finished workout emotion event through MoodManager::TriggerEmotionEvent and then steps that pointer on by one 0x40-byte entry unless it already points at the last: r1 = end - 0x40, and the advance is predicated on current != last (0x00573E24). The constructor 0x00573BA8 clears the component and leaves the pointer at the first entry
evidence: this stack picked by index with medium as a default, which is neither the order the engine runs them in nor a default it has
ShouldPlayEightiesMusic 0x00573E30 caches its answer in a flag at +0x11 and otherwise scores the current workout mood scorer and rolls RandDbl(1.0) against a constant

records.title: The three path segment messages are a Planning::PathSegment copied field for field
records.authority: PathDolerOuter::Dole 0x00507E4C switches on the segment type at PathSegment+0 (1 line, 2 arc, 3 point turn) and copies the struct straight into the message: words at +4, +8, +0xC, +0x10 (and +0x14 for an arc), then the speed profile at +0x1C, +0x20, +0x24, then for a point turn the byte at +0x14. The fields are named by their definers - PathSegment::DefineLine 0x0085BC00 (x_start, y_start, x_end, y_end), DefineArc 0x0085BC98 (x_center, y_center, radius, start, sweep), DefinePointTurn 0x0085BD28 (x, y, target angle, tolerance, and a bool at +0x14) - and SetSpeedProfile 0x0085BC90 writes target speed, acceleration and deceleration at +0x1C
records.effect: the robot drives a different path from the one the planner produced
records.provenance: read from the engine; this stack already sent the same values in the same order
evidence: VizManager::AppendPathSegmentLine(unsigned int, float, float, float, float) and AppendPathSegmentArc(unsigned int, float x 5) corroborate the geometry by their own signatures
DefineLine also stores atan2(dy, dx) at +0x14 and DefineArc a computed end angle at +0x18; neither goes on the wire
